searchText: The 64x smaller aggregate committee attestation size translates to a relatively significant reduction in network bandwidth, correct? That seems to be a big benefit if I’m understanding this correctly. No, currently honest aggregators should only publish aggregated attestations with aggregation bits' length to be the size of its own committee. It's only for malicious actors that fill up the aggregation bits to max length, which is 63x of useless info, that need to be deserialized by others before performing the validation. So bandwidth saving only on committee bits. And malicious actors can only fill aggregation bits with `MAX_VALIDATORS_PER_COMMITTEE`. Anything longer with be ignored by peers it would have to be malicious validators though, right? not just any actor I think any node on p2p, so basically anyone We already have this validation in the `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` topic: ``` [REJECT] The number of aggregation bits matches the committee size -- i.e. `len(aggregation_bits) == len(get_beacon_committee(state, aggregate.data.slot, index))`. ``` This covers the problem of excessive aggregation bits, no? Isn't this after the ssz deserialization? I think if we have a container specifically for aggregated attestation, we can ignore/reject this case because we can't even deserialize the bytes into the appropriate container, instead of deserialize it first and then later find out the aggregation bits mismatch in the validation. anyone? this referred to the average block time in PoW ethereum it isn't really relevant anymore, esp after the Pectra hard fork

excerpts.author: radekkapka
excerpts.content:
We already have this validation in the `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` topic:
```
[REJECT] The number of aggregation bits matches the committee size -- i.e. 
  `len(aggregation_bits) == len(get_beacon_committee(state, aggregate.data.slot, index))`.
```
This covers the problem of excessive aggregation bits, no?

excerpts.author: nc1234
excerpts.content: Isn't this after the ssz deserialization? I think if we have a container specifically for aggregated attestation, we can ignore/reject this case because we can't even deserialize the bytes into the appropriate container, instead of deserialize it first and then later find out the aggregation bits mismatch in the validation.
